title: What are the looping constructs in Java?
shortTitle: What are the looping constructs in Java?
keyPoints: for loop: known iteration count, index access – for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
for-each (enhanced for): iterate over arrays or Iterable – for (Account a : accounts)
while: condition checked before each iteration – while (hasNext())
do-while: body runs at least once, condition checked after – do { ... } while (condition)
break exits the loop entirely, continue skips to the next iteration
Labeled break/continue for nested loops – break outer; skips both loops

s1_definition.oneliner: Java has four loops: for (counter-based), for-each (collection iteration), while (pre-check), and do-while (post-check, runs at least once).
s1_definition.profdef:
Four loop constructs:

- **for:** Best when you know the iteration count or need an index. `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)`.
- **for-each:** Best for iterating arrays and collections without an index. `for (Account a : accounts)`.
- **while:** Condition checked before each iteration. The body may never run. `while (scanner.hasNext())`.
- **do-while:** Body runs at least once, condition checked after. `do { retry(); } while (!success)`.
s1_definition.analogy: A bank teller processing a queue. The for loop says: "Process exactly 10 customers." The for-each says: "Process every customer in the queue." The while says: "Keep processing while there are customers waiting." The do-while says: "Process at least one customer, then check if more are waiting."

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  for (init; condition; update)    for (T item : collection)
    init → check → body → update     iterator → hasNext? → body → next
    → check → body → update → ...     → hasNext? → body → next → ...

  while (condition)                do { body } while (condition)
    check → body → check → ...        body → check → body → check → ...
    (may never run)                    (always runs at least once)

  break:    exits the loop entirely
  continue: skips to the next iteration
  break label: exits the labeled outer loop
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Java has four loop constructs. The for loop is best when you know the iteration count or need an index. The for-each loop is cleanest for iterating collections and arrays. The while loop checks the condition first and may never execute the body. The do-while loop always executes the body at least once, then checks.

Break exits the loop entirely. Continue skips to the next iteration. Labeled break exits a named outer loop from inside a nested inner loop.

One sentence to remember: use for when you have a counter, for-each when you have a collection, while when you have a condition, and do-while when the body must run at least once.
